title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Top block: as transcribed, 'a\X → b\X' should be 'a\X → b\Y'.
Top block: 'à fibres non objet initial' is garbled; it should read 'fibres having an initial object' to match the third equivalent condition.
The heading 'f ∈ E' is inconsistent with the later summary 'C ⊊ Pr', 'C = F^0'. The first class is presumably C (precofibred), or E is a separate name used once.

Variance conventions (X_b → X_{/b} vs X_b → b\X; aspherical vs coaspherical) differ from those later fixed by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. As written, the cofibred case is stated via X_{/b}, whereas the Cisinski-style convention ties opfibrations to b\X. The direction should be checked, but the overall duality scheme is coherent.
'WSC ∩ Pr ⊂ S' presumably means WSE ∩ Pr. In 3bis the struck 'WSE' was replaced by WSB.
The query 'mais non par g ∈ S ?' is left open: stability of WSE under base change by sharp maps is not settled on the page.

ideas.what: Proper functors characterised by aspherical fibres of a\X → b\Y, aspherical lift categories, and Rf_* commuting with arbitrary base change; smooth as the dual
ideas.modern_name: W-proper / W-smooth functors; proper and smooth base change for Cat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs), developed by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005) and Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006); ∞-version in Lurie HTT §4.1 and Cisinski's 2019 book
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (proper/smooth maps of Cat); Les Dérivateurs

ideas.what: Class S: functors along which pullback preserves weak equivalences; self-dual
Sm ∩ Pr ⊂ S and (locally trivial) ∩ Pr/Sm ⊂ S
ideas.modern_name: Ehresmann-type theorem: smooth proper functors are homotopically locally trivial; bifibrations are sharp

ideas.what: Quillen Theorem B hypothesis (X/b → X/b' in W) equivalent to sharpness of the cofibred replacement, and to pullback preserving W between smooth objects over Y; cohomological shadow 'Rf_* of constants locally constant'
ideas.modern_name: Theorem B / homotopy locally constant functors; sharpness of the Grothendieck-construction replacement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1973); Cisinski's 'W-localement constant' treatment of Theorem B

ideas.what: Two-sided Theorem B condition via two-sided commas b0'\X/b1 (class WSB), equivalent to both one-sided conditions holding locally
ideas.modern_name: two-sided / twisted-arrow version of Quillen's Theorem B

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a symmetric 'weakly sharp' theory: WSE (Theorem-B type, stable under smooth base change) and dual WSF (stable under proper base change). He claims WSE∩Pr ⊂ S and WSF∩Sm ⊂ S, and asks whether WSE is stable under base change by arbitrary sharp maps.
missed.quote: stable par chgt de base par fl. lisses (mais non par g∈S ?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A clean statement of the base-change stability of Theorem-B classes, and of the interaction 'weakly sharp + proper ⇒ sharp', could be useful in ∞-categorical proper/smooth base change theory. The open question is not obviously settled in print.

missed.claim: A two-sided Theorem B condition (WSB) using double comma categories b0'\X/b1, claimed equivalent to the local conjunction of the left and right Theorem B conditions.
missed.quote: pour b'_0 → b_0 →u b_1 → b'_1 dans Y, b'_0\X/b_1 → b'_0\X/b'_1 est ∈ W
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Two-sided / twisted-arrow homotopy local constancy is relevant to bimodule/profunctor fibrations. I do not know of this exact equivalence stated in the Cat-localizer literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Most content (proper/smooth functors, base change, dualities, Theorem B) is in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs and was systematised by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski. Less familiar details are the explicit equivalences: Theorem B hypothesis ⇔ sharpness of the cofibred replacement ⇔ W-preservation under pullback between smooth objects. The two-sided WSB variant and the open stability question are mildly novel, but the treatment is sketchy.
